name: Smith Machine Front Squat
description: The Smith machine front squat positions the bar across the front deltoids and clavicles, guided by the machine's fixed vertical track. The guided bar path removes the balance demands of a free-weight front squat, allowing the lifter to focus entirely on quad depth and torso position. The front rack position promotes an upright torso and maximal quadriceps recruitment.

execution.starting_position: Position the Smith machine bar across the front deltoids (front rack position). Cross the arms over the bar or use a clean grip. Feet shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly, feet positioned slightly forward of the bar.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the Smith machine bar at upper-chest height. Step under and position bar on front delts. Rotate the bar to unlock.
steps: Step 1: Brace the core and keep the elbows high throughout the movement.
Step 2: Bend the knees and squat down, keeping the torso very upright.
Step 3: Descend until thighs are at or below parallel.
Step 4: Drive through the feet to return to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent. Exhale at the top.
common_mistakes: Elbows dropping, allowing the bar to roll off the delts
Insufficient ankle mobility causing heel rise
safety_considerations: Ensure elbow flexibility for the front rack — use a crossed-arm grip if needed
The Smith machine's fixed path can stress the knees if foot position is incorrect
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full depth — hip crease below the knee. The upright torso makes this more achievable.
